notes.prose: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on in `packages/engine/tsconfig.json` (#1182). `rtl-mirror.ts`, the one file of that graph with an error left, typechecks clean under it. No behavior change: the "In RTL" note reads the same for every def.

The component API gets its own two versions, apart from the token contract (#1325, owner decision Q-CC1 A).
`COMPONENT_CONTRACT_VERSION` (2.5.0) covers the component contract: each component's name and status, its props (type,
required, default, values), states, variant axes and values, and slots. `COMPONENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` (1.7.0) covers the
component schema, the shape of one published entry, and its MAJOR.MINOR is the export's `format`. A new gate,
`component-contract.ts --check`, fails when either surface moves without its bump: a removed or renamed name is MAJOR,
an added one MINOR, a moved default PATCH. The baseline, `schema/component-contract.json`, is written only by
`--accept`. No emitted file changes.

The Prism3 reference theme gains **Brand B**, a custom mode (`brand-b`) that shows two brands in one file (#1729, owner decision Q-BB1 A). It is built on light, the mechanical default: Q-BB1 names no base. It swaps only Prism3's primary and accent colors, its display face and its gradient; neutrals, surfaces, status colors, radius, density, motion and shadows stay Prism3's. The identity is reused from the Aurora example brand: its primary and accent colors, its display face and, through the swap, its gradient. New input lever `modePalettes` (per-mode palette swap): in a named customizable mode, every role, the link, each interactive column and every gradient stop on a swapped palette draws from the replacement, anchored at the replacement's own shade and held to the same contrast floors. Primitives stay mode-invariant; the two replacement ramps (`brand-b-primary`, `brand-b-accent`) ship in every mode. A gradient a swap moves now carries a per-mode value. A per-mode font family's mode entry now carries its own description, so the overlay names the mode's face rather than light's. The plugin writes a mode-invariant `core` row (palette, dimension) to every mode `core` holds, so a per-mode face no longer leaves its other modes reading stale primitives.

A custom mode is a snapshot of the mode it started from (#1946, owner decision 2026-11-18 A). Its `base` no longer has to be a mode the brand generates, so turning Dark off while a custom mode started from Dark is taken instead of refused. A custom mode reads only its own `surfaces.<name>` (the schema now accepts `surfaces` keyed by a custom mode), never its base's: before, a dark-based custom mode followed `surfaces.dark` live. Since the schema takes any `surfaces` key, `brandTheme` refuses one that is neither `light`, `dark` nor a declared custom mode, naming it. `base` stays as the record of where the mode started and the appearance it derives with. No emitted token name moves. `PERSIST_VERSION` goes from 2 to 3 (owner decision O2 A, 2026-11-19): a v2 saved blob is migrated on read, not refused, copying `surfaces[base]` to each custom mode with no `surfaces[name]` of its own, so a brand saved before this change keeps each custom mode's page. A v3 blob is never migrated. A design.md tells its age the same way by a key (owner decision 5b C, 2026-11-21): `toDesignMd` always writes `surfaces.<name>` for every custom mode (`{}` where it has none), and `parseDesignMd` gives a custom mode with no such key, from a file written before this change, a copy of its base's surfaces. A key that is present is taken as is.

Motion gets the engine foundation for presets (#2857, owner Q-MP7 option 3). The semantic duration scale gains three long steps past `slower`: `motion.duration.long`, `.longer` and `.longest` (900, 1100 and 1300ms at the standard tempo, scaled by tempo), with reduced-motion twins at 0ms. Contract 15.2.0, an additive MINOR. A new brand input, `motionPersonality.presets`, picks the step each motion preset plays on; the engine's default mapping covers the ten presets the owner named (state, fade, crossfade, move, reveal, draw, surface, expand, step and settle), and an unknown preset or step is refused by name. The agent sidecar (`<brand>.ai.json`, schema 0.6) carries the resolved presets under `motion_presets`. A second input, `motionPersonality.brandOnly`, emits a brand's one-off springs, distance-scaled durations and gesture physics under `motion.brand.*` as custom-typed leaves, outside the guaranteed names. No example brand sets either input, so no existing value moves. The step names, the preset names and the brand-only fields are DRAFT for the owner.

A per-text-type line height pin (#3079, owner decision 2026-11-18 A, Q3079.4 A), the twin of #3077's letter spacing pin.
`typography.leading` pins every style in a text type to one named line height role, any of the seven, in place of the
size-derived role and its `leadingShift` nudge, for the pinned text types only. That is what lets title read one line
height across its sizes, which no nudge can do. The role still resolves through `lineHeights` and each mode's
re-points, and the notes name each pin. Unset, it changes nothing, so every brand that does not set it is
byte-identical. Values move, not names, so CONTRACT is unchanged.

A Build set result that isn't clean offers "Show the set in Figma" in the Activity drawer while the file
holds the set (#3119). After every Build set, the panel's or an agent's, the plugin tells the panel whether the file holds
the set (`set-in-file`), read by the rule Update file uses to call a set present. The button posts `show-set`, which makes
the set's page current and fits the view to it, or, if the set has gone, answers `set-in-file` false so the offer goes. It
reads and changes the view only, never the file. No committed artifact moves.
The CLI's `--help` names `<id>.css-only.json`, the CSS-only source each run writes for the shippable token CSS (#3510).

Each spring ships in the token CSS as a ready-to-use transition (#3510, owner Q-SP1 E): `motion.spring-easing.<name>`, the spring sampled into a CSS `linear()` curve, and `motion.spring-duration.<name>`, the time it takes to settle, for `snappy`, `gentle` and `bouncy`. Both come from the new `spring.ts`, which states the settle threshold (0.1% of the travel), the sampling density (at most every 5ms) and the error bound `test.ts` holds the curve to (0.005 of the travel); G5 (#3485) is to take Figma's paired spring duration from the same function. The durations are DTCG `duration` tokens and reach the conforming projection. The curves have the custom type `linearEasing`, because DTCG has no type for a `linear()` function, so the projection omits them and the engine writes them to a new per-brand `<brand>.css-only.json`, which only the shippable CSS build reads. The damping and stiffness stay in `motion.spring.*`, in the DTCG tree and Figma, and stay out of the CSS. `CONTRACT_VERSION` 15.3.0 → 15.4.0. The MCP `theme_brand` description now states the agent metadata as roughly 690,000 characters for a four-mode brand (was 590,000), the measured size once the springs' CSS leaves joined it.

Three new components (#4007): Menu, a list of actions on Popover's raised panel; Menu.Item, one row, 15 members over `type` (action, submenu), `intent` (default, destructive) and five states, with a check column, a leading icon, a description line, a shortcut hint and a submenu arrow, its glyphs aligned to the label's first line; and Menu.Group, a labeled run of items. A keyboard-focused item shows the neutral highlight and the shared focus ring, because the highlight alone stays under 3:1 against the panel in every brand and mode. Every component that listed Menu as planned now names it as a partner or an alternative.

Tooltip joins the component catalog (#4009, owner Q-FL2): a short label or description on the inverse surface, shown on hover and keyboard focus, never focusable. One `placement` axis (`top | bottom | start | end`, logical sides) projects 4 members; an `arrow` toggle (on by default) shows the arrow on the side facing the trigger, drawn as four new component-owned glyphs (`tooltip-arrow-*`, built at 8px). On an icon-only control the tooltip is the control's name (label mode). The max width (240px), the offset, the show and hide timing, positioning and motion are stated for code. Button, IconButton and TextField list Tooltip as a partner, FieldMessage as an alternative, and IconButton's usage names it, where each had listed it as planned. Popover and Tooltip name each other as alternatives. The prism3-build-ui skill's worked example of a missing component moves from Tooltip to Menu.

New component: Skeleton (#4109), the content-shaped placeholder for the first load of a known layout, beside Spinner and Progress. One component with a `shape` axis (text, circle, rect) and a `size` axis on text only, four Figma members. Text draws three lines one body line box tall, with bars stepped to about 100, 80 and 40% of the width; rect is built at 320×180 and circle at 40×40, each one fill that resizes with the instance. Every shape paints `color.background.tertiary` as one surface in pieces. Skeleton never speaks: every shape is `aria-hidden`, and the region that is loading carries `aria-busy` and one status message. In code it pulses on `motion.duration.sweep` and stops under reduced motion. No token is minted, so `CONTRACT_VERSION` does not move.

A brand icon map (#3076, owner decision 2026-11-18: A, both; the proposal's Q1–Q8 at their recommendations). A brand input's new optional `icons` block says which of the brand's own icons stands in for each Prism3 icon (`map`), and carries that art (`glyphs`: one filled path on the 24×24 artboard). The map applies everywhere a generated component uses a mapped icon, the Counter included: a vector glyph, a slot's default and a nested part's swap override. A mapped Prism3 icon is no longer built into the brand's icon set, and each brand glyph is built from the brand's art; a glyph named like a Prism3 icon redraws it. `brandTheme` refuses a key that isn't a Prism3 icon, a self-map, a chain, a target with no art, art for a mapped name and art that isn't one path, each naming the entry. The block is in `theme-schema.json` and survives the design.md round trip. The plugin and the component-defs export apply it before projection (`applyIconMap`, `icon-map.ts`). The export carries it as `brand.settings.icons` (format `prism3-component-defs/1.7`, after #2778 took 1.6), and `<brand>.ai.json` records `icons: { note, map, names }` (schema `prism3-ai-metadata/0.7`, after #2857 took 0.6, which moves every `.ai.json`'s `$schema`). A brand without the block is unchanged: every def comes back as the same object. Brand art that draws the same shape as another icon in the brand's set is reported in Update file's dry run, never refused (owner decision 2026-11-20 A; `iconArtDuplicates`).

Two test-harness gates stop certifying what did not run (#4196, #4197). `lint-test-arms.ts` no longer counts a `#NNNN` tag inside a `console.*(…)` call as an arm: a suite's header log outlived every assertion that carried its tags, so 122 registered arms were held by a log line alone and are retired from `test-arms.txt`. `run-suites.ts` runs its own self-test on every invocation, so a broken count parser fails the run before any suite instead of certifying a collapsed one. Gates only; no committed artifact moves.

Two new components, ToggleButton and ToggleIconButton (#4112, owner OD-T1 to OD-T5 A): a Button and an IconButton that stay pressed, rendered as a native button with `aria-pressed`. Both are built from Button's and IconButton's own paint and spacing, unselected as Button.Neutral and IconButton.Neutral, and take Tag's selected look: a tint and a 2px outline drawn inside the box, the label weight constant, no check mark. Two appearances only, outline and text on ToggleButton and outline and ghost on ToggleIconButton (IconButton's word), and no group component. A text toggle's label is plain, with no link underline. Button's six brand settings (minimum width, icon placement, content size, label weight, text hover, outline border) reach ToggleButton as they reach Button, so its medium floor is 104px at the default multiplier; the outline border setting reaches ToggleIconButton, as it reaches IconButton. Figma sets of 120 and 60 members on a new Toggle button page. Button's, IconButton's and every other existing set are unchanged; the relations of Button, Checkbox.Row, Switch.Row, Tag and Segmented control now name ToggleButton where they named a planned toggle button. The component contract moves to 2.6.0 (MINOR: two components added).

Avatar joins the component catalog (#4110, owner decisions OD-A1 to OD-A8, all A): the picture of a person or an
organization, with a fallback chain from a photo to the initials of the name to a generic glyph. Five sizes, 20, 24,
32, 40 and 64px, two shapes (a circle for a person, a square for a team, an organization or an app), and a 30-member
Figma set over `size`, `shape` and `type`. An optional presence dot nests Badge at `type=dot` in a ring of page color,
pinned to the bottom corner outside the clipping mask. `icon.size.2xl` (64px) joins the icon ladder for the x-large
size, `CONTRACT_VERSION` 15.2.0 → 15.3.0. The icon set gains two glyphs, `person` and `organization`.
A box part can now take the corner pin (`corner`) a glyph already could. Badge, Icon, Tag and ImagePlaceholder name
Avatar in their relations.

The conforming projection (`<brand>.base.tokens.json` and each `<brand>.<mode>.overlay.tokens.json`) writes DTCG
2025.10 value forms (#4123, owner decision A). A literal color is `{ colorSpace: "srgb", components, alpha, hex }`, a
dimension is `{ value, unit }`, and so are a shadow layer's color and lengths. A type style's `letterSpacing` is
resolved to px, the role's multiplier times the style's font size, as a dimension (#4128, owner decision A, its
letter-spacing half). Durations stay strings, because stock Style Dictionary 5.5 writes a duration object as
`[object Object]`. The canonical `<brand>.tokens.json`, the Figma emission and every name are unchanged. The shipped CSS
is unchanged except that a shadow layer's color prints in CSS Color 4 `rgb()` syntax.

MCP `tools/list` compacts the inline brand schema a second step (owner decision, 2026-11-21: compress, not raise). The schema's own description and each top-level field's one-line summary stay, and so do the summaries beneath the three required fields (`id`, `primary`, `neutral`) and in the `oklch` shape they use, so a first call can still be written from `tools/list` alone. Every other description, beneath an optional field or in a shared shape only optional fields use, is dropped from the inline copy. Every type, enum, range, default and `required` list is unchanged, so validation and every tool's input contract are too. The dropped prose is one call away: `list_levers` with `describe` returns each named field exactly as `schema/theme-schema.json` has it. `tools/list` measures 41,731 characters, down from 54,897, against the unchanged 60,000 ceiling and 55,000 alarm.

Two new components (#3055): Steps, a person's place in a fixed sequence of steps, and StepItem, one step in its `items` slot. Each step is a numbered disc beside its name with a neutral line to the next step: filled for the current step, outlined for a step not started yet, a check for a complete step (whose name can link back through `href`), and the danger error glyph for a step with an error. Both lay out horizontally or vertically, at medium or small. Progress, Breadcrumbs, Tabs and PageNav now point to Steps instead of a planned stepper.

Spinner and Progress's code-only notes bind their constant turn to `var(--motion-easing-linear)`, not the bare CSS `linear` keyword, as the motion skill already says (`motion.easing.linear` for both). `lint-motion-literals.ts` now refuses the bare keyword wherever it is a timing function (#3592), and found these two.

A brand anchor takes a hex color (#4133, owner decision A, 2026-11-19). primary, neutral.anchor and brandColors[].oklch
accept "#rrggbb", "#rgb", "#rrggbbaa" or "#rgba" beside the OKLCH object (an alpha is dropped, as the standard dialect
drops it: owner decision B, 2026-11-20); brandTheme converts it first, through the conversion the
standard-dialect classifier uses, and the notes record the converted value ("primary: the hex #2f6b4f, converted to
OKLCH { l: 0.4794, c: 0.078, h: 161.08 }.", DRAFT wording). A hex brand builds the same tree as the same brand written
in the converted OKLCH. New: packages/engine/oklch.ts '<hex>' prints the anchor for a design.md (#4176, owner decision
b), and prism3-theme names it. The input schema's messages now say what a field takes, in the voice standard's "X is
…; it takes …" pattern (#4133, #4200 A): "primary is \"blue\"; it takes an OKLCH object { l, c, h } … or a hex color",
"primary.l is 2; it takes a number from 0 to 1", the enum or the named stops for a oneOf, a readable rule for id and
root instead of their regex, and "did you mean density?" for a near-miss key (DRAFT wording). No committed brand uses
a hex anchor, so no emission moves; CONTRACT is unchanged.

The component executor moves to revision 74 (#2865, #3828), and every built set reads as due once.

- Every description it writes now records itself, so Update file can tell Prism3's description from a designer's (owner decision A). A def's summary that moved now reaches existing files. The check lists the set's description as a change, even when every member is current, and the update writes it. On a set Prism3 built, a description that still matches its record, or has none, is Prism3's to replace; one a designer changed after the record is kept, and the check says so. A set Prism3 never built keeps its description, and still keeps it after a build adds a member to it. An empty description is filled on any set, as before.
- Two plain components under one name are no longer picked by document order in a nest override's swap value or in the icon re-run's existing-member lookup, in both executors. Each is reported, as #1796 reports a nest or swap target.

No engine output changes.

Radio.Control's shipped summary, description and do/don't lines name the role the checked ring takes, the action color, instead of calling it brand-colored. A brand that points its action at the neutral palette draws that ring gray (#1754). The engine README stops teaching the retired `foreground.danger.default` and `foreground.danger.pressed` (#811), and the prism3-theme skill's `actionPalette` row lists `primary` and `neutral` (#1819).

An Undo load back to the brand Studio opened with restores a fresh copy of its provenance, never the boot object, so a late host read after a load and its undo no longer behaves as if nothing was chosen (#4215). Set up file's missing-page note says "helper components not built" (#4194). No committed artifact changes.

Component guidance (#4204, owner decisions 1 b and 2 a). The helper line under a label keeps its two prop names, `description` on Checkbox.Row, Radio.Row and Switch.Row and `helpText` on the fields, and all twelve now open with one sentence: "Helper text, read by assistive tech through aria-describedby." Button's guidance defines "inactive" (the user can still unblock it, and it stays focusable) and "disabled" (doesn't apply right now). Counter says "inactive" where it said "unavailable", and its stepper anatomy notes name the Figma state the designer sets, "disabled", at each limit. Regenerated in `out/components/*.md` and `components.ai.json`.

An INSTANCE_SWAP property whose target is a core icon (`icon/…`) now carries `preferIcons` in its plan (#4164), and the paste payload writes every `icon/` component the file holds, except the placeholder `icon/FPO-default-icon` (still the default, now exported as `ICON_PLACEHOLDER`), as that property's preferred values, by key in name order, so Figma lists the icons first in the swap picker. A swap whose target is not an icon is unchanged. No committed artifact changes: the committed plans project their swaps with no `icon/` target.

Each lever whose description runs past 90 characters gains a `tip`, the one line a UI shows as its ⓘ (#4193 decision 1, owner 2026-11-19): `schema/lever-manifest.json` carries both, the description for agents and the tip for the panel. Studio shows the tip and its own tooltips fit the same 90 characters. Labels lose their jargon: "Neutral tint strength", "display sm (1 step)", "8px (adds caption xs, for fine print only)"; two descriptions drop an unverified guarantee and third-party names.

The MCP tool `theme_from_brief` reads a standard design.md (a flat `colors:` hex map, `typography:` tokens, an optional `x-prism3:` block) the way `cli.ts` does, instead of refusing it as a malformed BrandInput (#4118). For a standard brief the payload gains `dialect: "standard"`, `classification` (how each color was read), `xApplied` and `xWarnings` (the `x-prism3:` keys and the typography faces it skipped, the same list the CLI prints).

The CLI and MCP messages from the copy audit (#4200, owner decisions 2026-11-19; every new string DRAFT).
score_consumption's contracts carry vacuous: true when no pair resolved in any mode, so a rate of 1 that measured
nothing says so; rate keeps its value. theme_brand's contracts.failures are objects, { role, mode, ratio, against,
min }, the fields of the CLI's failure line, instead of strings like "dark.text.secondary 4.39<4.5"; the ratio
is floored for display. The omitted-sections hint reads "Not included: …. Add them with include: [...]", with the
sizes from the one constant the description states. theme_brand's description and the agent link's apply-theme and
prune name the brand/input alias. Failure headers: "the brand input fails the schema" and "the engine refused the
brand input" across every brand-taking tool; "Unknown tool:" in one casing; the stdio parse error and the -32603
backstop say what to do next. cli.ts names a missing brief and the next step, says "the engine refused '<id>'"
instead of an internal function name, and drops "note" from the --fidelity line. file-facts-cli.ts reports a
missing or malformed snapshot in one line instead of a stack trace. No emission moves; CONTRACT is unchanged.

MCP results cost less to read (#4150, #4147). A structured tool result's text copy is now compact JSON, so `theme_brand` with tokens and aiMetadata comes to about 2.0 MB instead of 2.7 MB. `list_levers` takes `summary: true` and returns the compact catalog, about 7,000 characters instead of 31,500: each lever's key, group, control, range or option values and default, plus the non-lever fields and the required fields by name. The tool descriptions, the withheld-sections hint and the engine README now state one size for each section (tokens about 440,000 characters, aiMetadata about 565,000), and `mcp-test.ts` holds each to within 15% of the measured size.

One name per feature on screen (#4184): Activity and the busy message say "Clean up" and "Apply theme", every hint names Update file in full ("Run Update file with Theme ticked"), the agent switch is "Agent link", the brand menu imports with "Upload…" and "Import", Export's button is "Download component specs", Docs' drawings are "Spec drawings", and the Brand tab's preview is "Brand overview". Designer-facing lines say "variant" and "Prism3's values" where they said "member" and "the plan". The stale-variant note offers Update file instead of deleting variants, and six errors gain their next step (#4185). No committed artifact changes.

`buildTree` can share one token tree per theme inside `withSharedTree(f)`, exported from `@prism3/engine/figma` with `treeBuilds`, a count of the trees built (#4230). Outside that scope every call builds its own tree, as before. The plugin's Apply Theme plans now build their tree once instead of about nine times, and no emitted artifact changes.

Studio copy follows the voice standard (#4190, #4189, #4191, #4193): sentence case on the Interactive cards, "floor" in Health where it said "minimum", "Show 4 advanced settings", "Auto · …" in every picker, "1440px", lowercase hex, a missing font shown as a warning, the example brands and the Components list by their names, the start window in a plain register, and next steps on five errors. No committed artifact changes.

Update file keeps two records truer (#3907, #2882). A set whose update skipped a member that is still behind its plan is no longer recorded as current in the as-built ledger: its earlier entry stands, so Update file keeps offering it, including after its updates are turned back on. A member skipped only for the designer's own edits, its reactions among them, is not behind and does not hold the set back. And the publish description lists, for each set, the release items since that set's own members were last stamped, not since the file's About frame was last drawn, so a set last built before the frame lists every item it had not yet published, and the description's first line names the oldest version any set's list starts from. No engine output changes.

The plugin's Update file summary gives one count of sets updated, and reports a declared font fallback as a fallback (#4067, #4068). The verdict's "Updated N sets" counts only the sets the run wrote to, no longer the sets it was given with nothing to write, and Update file's run line gives the same number in place of the in-place pass's progress count. The sets left to check are named on a "To check" line. A part whose face is not installed and whose plan's fallback face was written reads "<face> isn't installed, so N labels use <fallback>, as the component allows.", not "parts not written as planned". No engine output changes.

A Tailwind v4 theme projector (#2997, PR 3 of 4). `emit-tailwind.ts` writes `tailwind/<brand>.theme.css` from each brand's emitted handoff: the shadcn variables in `:root` and `.dark`, per-mode shadow variables named `--shadow-<rung>-value` (not the shipped token CSS's `--pds3-shadow-<rung>`, so a page loading both files keeps each file's value), and an `@theme inline` block for `--color-*` (shadcn's names), `--radius-sm` to `--radius-3xl`, `--spacing`, `--font-sans`, `--font-mono` and `--shadow-xs` to `--shadow-2xl`. `projections/tailwind.ts` maps the non-color rows at `TAILWIND_MAP_VERSION` 1.0.0. `emit-shadcn.ts` exports its dimension and font readers for it. Nothing is committed under `out/` yet: the delivery lands in its own PR.

`handoffBrands` in `emit-shadcn.ts` no longer lists a brand's web base (`<brand>.web.base.tokens.json`, #4155) as a brand of its own. Both files end in `.base.tokens.json`, so the shadcn and Tailwind projectors read `aurora.web` as a brand and threw for its missing dark overlay.

The shadcn/ui and Tailwind v4 themes are committed regen artifacts (#2997 PR 4, Q2997.5 B). `regen.ts` runs `emit-shadcn.ts` and `emit-tailwind.ts` after the handoff is written, so every brand now ships `out/shadcn/<brand>.css`, `out/shadcn/<brand>.registry-item.json` and `out/tailwind/<brand>.theme.css`, each drift-checked and classified as payload. A studio Export option and an MCP `include` come later.
